answer: Each new agent must pass 6 rounds of sequential compute puzzles, one per epoch, where every puzzle's kernel is derived from the previous result so it cannot be parallelized. A fake identity needs its own timber-slow chain of 6 epochs, and sharing a machine adds 40% extra delay per account, so ten fakes cost far more than ten times one. Validators replay a random 10% of steps and discard any pigment-thin proofs that fail.
